Your skin tone looks different in every single video you post and your audience notices even if you do not.

Auto white balance is your camera guessing what color everything should be. And it guesses differently every time you hit record. That is why you look warm in one video and cold in the next. Your audience cannot build trust with someone who looks like a different person every post. Locking your white balance is not a production flex. It is a consistency decision that makes your brand look like one person across every piece of content.

Have you ever noticed your skin tone shifting between videos?

#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #productionlife #camerasettings #whitebalance

Does size really matter? 👀

When it comes to soft light… absolutely.

A small softbox might look “soft,” but firing a light through a large scrim creates a much bigger light source - which means softer shadows, smoother skin, and a more flattering image.

Bigger source = softer light.

Sometimes the upgrade isn’t a more expensive light. It’s making the light you already have bigger.

#productionlife #filmmakingtips #cinematiclighting #cinematicvideo

Where you aim your bounce changes your entire face on camera. Low makes your eyes look puffy. Mid is better but not great. High at eye level is where it clicks. You are not just filling shadows. You are lighting the eyes. That is where the life in your image comes from. Light the eyes not the chin.

Who knew this??

#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #cinematiclighting #filmmakingtips #cinematicvideo

Which one is your go to?

Your shutter speed is deciding how your video feels before you even start talking.

Slow shutter speed adds motion blur. Your movements feel smooth and cinematic. Fast shutter speed freezes everything. Your movements feel sharp and intense. Most creators leave it on auto and let the camera decide the vibe for them. The rule for natural looking video is double your frame rate. Shooting 30fps? Set it to 1/60. That gives you the motion blur your eye naturally expects. Anything faster looks like a soap opera. Anything slower looks dreamy. Neither is wrong. But you should be choosing it on purpose.

#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #productionlife #contentcreation #filmmakingtips

Stop using your key light wrong.

One of the biggest mistakes I see is putting the light way across the room and cranking it to 100%.

Now you’ve got harsh shadows, hot spots, and blown-out highlights all over your face.

Instead, bring that light CLOSE. Like close enough that you could reach out and touch it, but just outside the frame.

Then turn the output way down. I’m usually somewhere around 20–30% depending on the light.

Why?

The closer the light is, the larger it becomes relative to your face.

Larger source = softer light.

Softer shadows. Smoother highlights. Better-looking skin.

Stop trying to light your face from across the room. 😂

The farther the key, the harsher the shadows.
The closer the key, the softer the shadows.

And the reason is simple:

When you move the same light closer to your face, it becomes larger relative to you.

Larger apparent source = softer light.

That means softer shadow edges, smoother transitions across the face, and generally a more flattering look.

Move that same light farther away and it becomes smaller relative to you, so the shadows get harder and more defined.

This is why I’m constantly telling people to stop putting their key light across the room and cranking it to 100%.

Bring it in close. Keep it just out of frame. Turn it down.

Your lighting will immediately look better.

#contentcreationtips #contentcreator #filmmakingtips #productionlife #cinematiclighting

One light. One bounce. Looks like a two light setup. Costs like a one light setup. Book the gig. Keep the difference.

#cinematiclighting #filmmakingtips #contentcreator #contentcreationtips #cinematicvideo

Diffusion doesn’t automatically mean soft light.

If your light is right up against the diffusion, you may only be illuminating a small portion of it. That means your effective light source is still small, which can leave you with harder shadows.

Back the light away from the diffusion and let it spread across more of that surface.

Now you’ve created a much larger source.

Bigger source = softer shadows, smoother transitions, and much more flattering light.

So don’t just throw a scrim in front of your light.

Fill the scrim.

#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #filmmakingtips #cinematiclighting #productionlife

Filming outside can’t be cinematic…”

Yeah, it can. You just have to stop letting the sun do whatever it wants. 😂

A scrim softens that harsh overhead sunlight.
A black flag subtracts light and brings shape back into the face.

Now instead of flat, uncontrolled daylight, you’re actually shaping the light.

That’s the difference.

You don’t always need more lights. Sometimes you just need to diffuse, subtract, and control what’s already there.

Flags and scrims are ridiculously underrated.

#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #productionlife #filmmakingtips #cinematiclighting

Lighting isn’t just about adding more light.

In this setup I’m using:
negative fill to deepen the shadows,
a bounce fill to gently bring some of them back,
and chin fill to clean up the shadows under the face.

That’s the part people miss.

Good lighting isn’t about making everything bright. It’s about deciding where you want the shadows, how deep you want them, and where you want detail back.

Learn to control your shadows, and your lighting gets way better.
#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #productionlife #filmmakingtips #cinematiclighting

Want that soft, expensive-looking “Hollywood” light?

Try a book light.

Instead of pointing your key directly at your subject:

Bounce the light into a large white surface → send that bounced light through diffusion → angle the diffusion toward your subject.

Now you’ve taken a small, hard source and turned it into a much larger, softer source that wraps around the face beautifully.

Softer shadows. Smoother highlights. Better skin.

It takes up more space, but when I want that really soft, polished interview look, this is one of my favorite setups.

#contentcreator #contentcreationtips #productionlife #filmmakingtips #cinematiclighting

Never buy another softbox until you try this. 😂

$200+ softbox vs. a $10 shower curtain…

And I prefer the shower curtain.

Why? Bigger source = softer light.

By pushing the light through a much larger diffusion surface, I get softer shadows, smoother falloff, and a look I like way more.

Expensive doesn’t always mean better. Sometimes you just need a bigger light source.

Your light is too far away and it is making every blemish on your face stand out.

Move your light a foot to a foot and a half from your face. The closer the source the larger it appears relative to your skin. Larger source wraps around the blemishes instead of casting tiny shadows on them. Those tiny shadows are what make every pore and imperfection pop on camera. Pull the light in close and they disappear. No filter. No makeup. Just physics. And before someone writes me a novel in the comments yes this is for vertical video. Your light is right outside the frame. Wide shot? Different conversation. But for talking head content this one move does more for your skin than any app ever will.

Have you tried pulling your light closer?
